summary: Syangboche Airport (SYH/VNSB) is a small mountain airstrip perched at approximately 3,780 meters (12,402 feet) in Nepal's Khumbu region, making it one of the highest airports in the world. It sits on a plateau above Namche Bazaar, the main trading hub and acclimatization stop for trekkers heading toward Everest Base Camp. The airport primarily serves small STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) aircraft and offers an alternative to the more famous but weather-sensitive Lukla airstrip.
faqs:
Q: What is the elevation of Syangboche Airport?
A: Syangboche Airport sits at approximately 3,780 meters (12,402 feet) above sea level, making it one of the highest airports in the world.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Syangboche Airport?
A: Small regional carriers such as Tara Air and Sita Air operate flights using STOL aircraft like the Dornier 228, typically connecting from Kathmandu via Lukla.

Q: Why is Syangboche Airport less commonly used than Lukla Airport?
A: While both serve the Everest region, Lukla is more frequently used because of higher passenger demand. Syangboche is sometimes preferred by trekking companies for logistics and as an alternative when Lukla weather is poor.

Q: How reliable are flights to Syangboche?
A: Flights are highly weather-dependent due to the surrounding Himalayan terrain. Delays and cancellations are common, especially during the monsoon season and winter.
transport_tips: From Kathmandu, travelers typically fly to Lukla first and then take a short mountain flight or helicopter transfer to Syangboche. Alternatively, some chartered helicopters fly directly from Kathmandu to Syangboche. From the airstrip, Namche Bazaar is just a short downhill trek of around 15 minutes, and most lodges and trekking agencies arrange porter-assisted transport of luggage. Plan for flexible schedules, as mountain weather frequently disrupts flight times.
local_tip: Book a window seat on the left side of the aircraft when flying in from Kathmandu for breathtaking views of Everest, Lhotse, and Ama Dablam as the plane descends into the Khumbu Valley.
